claims.claim: In the v1 world the deployed stuck hazard beats both the online base rate and frozen time-since-progress on log loss
In the v1 world the model is calibrated: the slope interval contains 1 and the intercept interval contains 0
In the shifted worlds the deployed model is worse than the better naive baseline in at least 2 of 3 families
The guard raises no flag in at least 7 of 8 v1 deployments
The guard flags at least 6 of 8 where the model is worse and at most 1 of 8 where it is clearly better
Premium: in the v1 world the guarded system is within 0.01 nats of always trusting the model
Payout: where the model is worse than the fallback by more than 0.05 nats the guard saves more than 0.02 nats against always-model
Time to progress, v1 world: the head's truncated CRPS beats the Kaplan-Meier constant
Error risk, no drift: the model beats the online base rate and its calibration slope interval contains 1
Error risk: the guard flags a rule change when the post-change model is worse than the fallback, and stays quiet when it is not or when nothing changed

tte_v1.unit: seconds, truncated CRPS over the observed 30-second steps (lower is better)
